newsitem.title: UK: Stakis Q2 hotel occupancy rate falls.
newsitem.headline: Stakis Q2 hotel occupancy rate falls.

text.p: Hotel and leisure group Stakis Plc said on Thursday its hotels, excluding the Metropole chain, showed an occupancy level of 64.7 percent in the 13 weeks to March 30, down from 69.1 percent in corresponding period last year.
But its average room rate was 50.96 stg, up from 45.69 stg in the second quarter of 1996.

Occupancy rate for the first half of the current financial year for its hotels, excluding the Metropole, chain was 68.2 percent, down from 70.8 percent the year before. Its average room rate for the first half was 50.51 stg, up from 45.59 stg.

The second quarter fall in occupancy rate was "attributable to the temporary closure of the Stakis Tyneside Hotel, a third of the St Ermins Hotel and other rooms off for redevelopment and refurbishment," the company said in a statement.
The 327 million stg acquisition of the Metropole hotels was completed last November and first began trading under the Stakis flag for six weeks in the first quarter of the current year.

The occupancy rate for Metropole in the 13 weeks to March 30 was 65.0 percent, up from 61.7 percent in the corresponding period the year before. Average room rate in the quarter was 72.66 stg, up from 65.33.
Metropole's occupancy rate for the half year was 64.9 percent, up from 60.6 percent. The average room rate was 70.28 stg, up from 63.42 stg.
Stakis said the comparative figures for Metropole were taken from the previous owners' management accounts. Occupancy rose 5.3 percent in the quarter and by 7.1 percent in the six month period.
Turnover at the group's casinos was 15.0 million stg in the second quarter, up from 13.0 million stg in the previous year. Turnover for the half year was 29.2 million stg, up from 24.8 million.
In its health and leisure business, Stakis said it has a new four year contract to manage 30 Hilton leisure clubs.
